```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

df = pl.read_csv("names_year_csv.csv")
```

# Best attempt at Elliot Chart:


```{python}
name = "Elliot"

name_history = (
    df
    .filter(pl.col("name") == name)
    .select(["year", "Total"])
    .sort("year")
    .filter(pl.col("year") >= 1950)
)

releases = {
    "year": [1982, 1985, 2002],
    "label": ["E.T. Released", "Second Release", "Third Release"]
}

(
    ggplot(name_history, aes(x="year", y="Total"))
    + geom_line(color="Blue", manual_key="Elliot")
    + labs(
        title="Elliot...What?",
        x="year",
        y="",
        manual="name",
        font="Times New Roman"
    )
    + geom_vline(
        xintercept=1982,
        color="Red",
        linetype="dashed",
        layer_key="E.T. Released"
        )
    + geom_vline(
        xintercept=1985,
        color="Red",
        linetype="dashed",
        label="Second Release"
    )
    + geom_vline(
        xintercept=2002,
        color="Red",
        linetype="dashed",
        label="Third Release"
    )
    + geom_text(
        data=releases,
        mapping=aes(x="year", label="label"),
        y=name_history["Total"].max() * 0.9,
        inherit_aes=False,
        family="Times New Roman"
    )
    + scale_x_continuous(format=".0f")
    + scale_y_continuous(format=".0f")
    + theme_gray()
)
```
